simple.meaning: לָחַשׁ (lâchash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to whisper ; by implication, to mumble a spell (as a magician).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in 2 Samuel, Psalms, beginning at 2 Samuel 12:19. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָחַשׁ (H3907) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לָחַשׁ (lâchash) / H3907 is traced through 2 Samuel 12:19, Psalms 41:8, Psalms 58:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said to his servants, “Is the child dead?”

definitions.short: to whisper ; by implication, to mumble a spell (as a magician)
definitions.full: H3907. lachash [ לָחַשׁ ] verb whisper, charm (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic לְחַשׁ ; Ethiopic ; whisper , see RS JPh xiv. 1885, 122, possibly originally serpent-charming); — Pi`el Participle plural מְלַחֲשִׁים קוֺל Psa 58:6 voice of whisperers (i.e. serpent-charmers ; || תֲבָרִים חוֺבֵר ). Hithpa`el whisper together , Imperfect יִתְלַחֲשׁוּ with עַל Psa 41:8 ; Participle plural מִתְלַחֲשִׁים 2Sam 12:19 .
